name: Latvia
summary: Independent in 1918, annexed by the Soviet Union in 1940, independent again in 1991 after the “Singing Revolution”; an EU and NATO member since 2004.

knownFor.label: Riga Art Nouveau
knownFor.note: One of the largest collections of Art Nouveau buildings.

knownFor.label: Baltic Way
knownFor.note: A human chain across the three Baltic states.

location.value: Baltic state; area 64,589 km² in the infobox, 64,573 km² in the introduction and 64,559 km² in the geography section.

terrain.value: Low plains, forests (over half the land), lakes and the Daugava River.

climate.value: Cool and damp, with cold winters and mild summers.

disasters.value: Supermarket roof collapse in Riga (2013), 54 dead.

population.value: 1,842,226 in a 2022 estimate (infobox); Latvians are 65.5% and Russians 24.1% (2025).

urbanisation.value: About 68% urban; Riga has about 600,000 people.

disease.value: Life expectancy is about 75 years, lower than in Western Europe.

migration.value: Mass deportations to Siberia in the 1940s; Russian-speaking settlers in Soviet times.

economicBase.value: A high-income, advanced economy: 2025 GDP about $47.9 billion nominal ($25,630 per person) and $82.4 billion PPP. Transport, logistics and timber are not named in the part of the page read.

tradeRoutes.value: Ports of Riga and Ventspils; EU single market since 2004.

wealth.value: Joined NATO and the EU in 2004 and adopted the euro on 1 January 2014; HDI 0.889, very high (41st in the infobox, 39th in the introduction).

moneyAndTax.value: The lats was introduced in 1993; Latvia adopted the euro in 2014.

inequality.value: Income inequality is among the higher levels in the EU.

keyRulers.value: Independence was declared on 18 November 1918, the Soviet Union incorporated Latvia on 5 August 1940, and independence was restored on 21 August 1991.

succession.value: Elections; the Saeima elects the president.

eliteConflict.value: Party politics; the Russian-speaking minority’s parties are usually kept out of government.

armyAndTech.value: A NATO member since 2004, with allied troops stationed in Latvia since 2017.

majorWars.value: German forces attacked Soviet troops on 22 June 1941 and controlled the country by early July; the Soviets reoccupied it in 1944–45.

territoryChange.value: Independence declared on 18 November 1918 (recognised 26 January 1921); occupied by Soviet forces in June 1940 and incorporated on 5 August 1940; independence restoration declared on 4 May 1990 and fully restored on 21 August 1991.

alliancesRivals.value: A member of the EU and NATO, and wary of Russia.

inventions.value: No major inventions; jeans rivets were patented by Latvian-born Jacob Davis (1873).

scienceEducation.value: University of Latvia (1919); Riga Technical University.

openness.value: A very open economy that trades widely within the EU.

communicationTransport.value: Railways, ports, Rail Baltica under construction.

religion.value: In 2018 the infobox gives 64% Christian (Lutheran 36%, Catholic 17%, Orthodox 9%) and 35% no religion, while the body text says Christianity is 79%, so the figures conflict.

languageWriting.value: Latvian, a Baltic language; Russian minority.

artsArchitecture.value: Art Nouveau buildings of Riga; song and dance festivals.

sharedIdentity.value: A strong national identity kept alive through song festivals and language.

dailyLife.value: Flats and wooden houses; rye bread, potatoes, fish.

neighbours.value: Neighbouring Baltic states, Russia, Poland, the Nordic countries.

ideasReligions.value: The Baltic Way, a human chain across the three Baltic states in 1989, demanded independence.

colonisation.value: Part of the Russian Empire and the USSR.

riseSignals.value: The independent Republic of Latvia was established on 18 November 1918.

outcome.value: Soviet forces occupied Latvia in June 1940; independence was restored on 21 August 1991. NATO and EU membership came in 2004 and the euro in 2014.
